_comment: Prompt for ApplyFactletWorker (in-process APPLY_FACTLET, one call per factlet batch). Placeholders: {trade} {geography} {buyerRoles} {audienceSegments} {notBuyer} = VALUE_PROP slice; {factletSource} {factletDate} {factletContent} = the factlet; {clientsLine} = clientsSome/clientsNone below; {sweepLine} = sweepRule/noSweepRule below. Output contract: the STRICT JSON shape on the last line is parsed by code -- change wording freely, never the shape.
lines: You are applying one sales-intelligence FACTLET to candidate CLIENTS for a "{trade}" vendor.

For EACH client decide if the factlet has sales-intelligence value for selling "{trade}" to that client or clients like them. LEAN RELEVANT; a false negative costs more than a false positive. RELEVANT if it provides ANY of: an event/occasion matching audienceSegments (need not name the client); demand for the trade or adjacent (RFP, seeking vendors, implied is fine); a NAMED contact person with a role at THAT client; geography placing the client inside/outside the service area; trade/buyer-profile intel (incl. notBuyer negatives). NOT relevant only if clearly unrelated, a name-collision (different org sharing a name token -- check company/website/bookings), or a verbatim duplicate of the client's dossierTail.

If the factlet describes a FUTURE dated event NOT already among a client's bookings, include a booking (omit "id" to CREATE; copy an existing booking's "id" to UPDATE it). Include email/phone/zip/date parts ONLY if they appear verbatim in the factlet text -- the server verifies and drops anything it cannot find there.
Return STRICT JSON only, no prose, exactly this shape:
sweepRule: SWEEP rule: if the factlet clearly names a REAL prospective client (an in-trade org or person, never a competitor vendor) AND a future bookable event (a date and a place), return it in "newClient". Otherwise newClient=null.
noSweepRule: newClient must be null (candidates were provided).
